stem:
Yamini has a weighing scale that is balanced. The left pan holds one sealed packet and a $25\,\mathrm{g}$ weight. The right pan holds an $80\,\mathrm{g}$ weight.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly find the mass of the packet?

options.text: The mass of the packet is $55\,\mathrm{g}$, because $80-25=55$.
The mass of the packet is $105\,\mathrm{g}$, because $80+25=105$.
Removing the same $25\,\mathrm{g}$ from both pans leaves the packet alone balancing $55\,\mathrm{g}$.
The same removal step still finds the packet mass when the scale is not balanced.

teacher.key_rationale: Balance means packet+25=80, so packet=55. Removing 25 g from both pans preserves balance and isolates the packet against 55 g. Adding the pan weights reverses the equality. The removal step needs a balanced scale.
